run.type: manual first run (Claude acting as each desk in one session)

documents.summary: Brent up ~13% in October on Middle East hostilities (US, Israel, Iran) disrupting crude flows.
Brent back at $110 on a missile attack near a Saudi oil port, Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, reduced Russian refining.
Oil jumps on escalating tanker attacks in the Middle East.
FOMC holds the target range at 3.75-4.00% (IORB 3.90%).
Fed holds in a 10-2 vote with hawkish dissent; markets price a December hike; September meeting hiked 25bp.
Shiller CAPE monthly reading 41.07 for October 2026; daily estimate 41.62 on Oct 8; peak 44.19 in Dec 1999.
S&P 500 CAPE ~41, highest since the dot-com bubble.
Spot gold fell to about $4,016/oz, lowest since July 20, 2026; steepest weekly fall in four months.
Versus last month, gold down 5.69% and silver down 17.47%.
Metals weaker on rising crude, inflation concerns and expectations of another Fed hike before year-end.

research.summary: Liquidity is draining at the margin but conditions are still loose. US net liquidity fell $79bn over 13 weeks as the Treasury holds about $1tn of cash and the reverse-repo buffer is gone, so reserves are doing the draining. Financial conditions stay easy and M2 grows near 6%. The dollar is firm; the yen has strengthened 4% in three months, a carry-unwind watch item.

key_findings.claim: US net liquidity (Fed assets - TGA - reverse repo) is $5,746bn, down $79bn in 13 weeks.
Treasury cash is about $1,000bn and reverse repo only $4.4bn, so reserves fell $91bn in 13 weeks.
Financial conditions are loose (NFCI -0.49) and M2 is up 5.71% year on year.
The broad dollar sits at its 78th percentile of 10 years; USD/JPY fell 4.18% in 3 months.

risks: Yen-funded carry unwind if USD/JPY keeps falling
TGA rebuild drains reserves further
what_would_change_my_mind: TGA falls below $850bn or the Fed's balance sheet starts growing again

research.summary: The Fed is in a hiking cycle: it raised rates in September and held at 3.75-4.00% in October with two hawkish dissents, and the 2-year yield sits 73bp above Fed funds, pricing more hikes. Real 10-year yields of 2.63% are restrictive. Long-run inflation expectations remain anchored. Credit spreads widened 18bp in a month but remain moderate. The hurdle rate is 3.88%.

key_findings.claim: Effective Fed funds is 3.88%, up 24bp in six months; the October meeting held with hawkish dissent.
The 2-year yield (4.61%) is 73bp above Fed funds, implying further hikes are priced.
The 10-year real yield is 2.63%, up 22bp in three months; 5y5y inflation expectations are anchored at 2.22%.
High-yield spreads widened 18bp in a month to 3.26%.

views.statement: TLT closes below 92 (about 12% above today) on its December expiry

risks: Flight to quality on a Gulf escalation could rally long bonds
A growth scare could flip the Fed quickly
what_would_change_my_mind: A weak October payrolls print with rising unemployment, or 2-year yields falling back below Fed funds
data_requests: Fed funds futures strip (implied path by meeting)
Full-history ICE BofA spreads (FRED keeps only 3 years)

research.summary: Growth is positive but fading and inflation is re-accelerating. Claims are low, GDPNow is 3.2% and the Philly Fed is strong, but payroll growth has slowed to 51k a month. Headline CPI is 4.0% as energy feeds through, core CPI is running 3.4% annualized over three months, and one-year inflation expectations are 4.6%. The growth composite slipped from 0.38 to 0.25 while inflation rose from 0.17 to 0.52.

key_findings.claim: Growth composite 0.25, down from 0.38 three months ago; payrolls 3-month average only 51k.
Labor market still tight on claims: 4-week average 197k, down 13.2% year on year; unemployment 4.2%.
Inflation composite rose from 0.17 to 0.52: headline CPI 4.02% y/y, core CPI 3.41% annualized over 3 months.
Consumers expect 4.6% inflation over the next year.

risks: September is the latest monthly data; October CPI and payrolls arrive in November
what_would_change_my_mind: October payrolls negative or claims above 250k

research.summary: Geopolitical risk is at decade highs. The 30-day Geopolitical Risk index is at its 93rd percentile of 10 years, driven by the US-Israel-Iran conflict, attacks around the Strait of Hormuz and on Saudi infrastructure. Oil supply is the main channel. US midterm elections on November 3 add policy uncertainty, already elevated at the 79th percentile.

key_findings.claim: 30-day average GPR is 175, at the 93rd percentile of 10 years and up 14 points in three months.
Attacks near a Saudi oil port and in the Strait of Hormuz pushed Brent back to $110 in mid-October; tanker attacks escalated.
US economic policy uncertainty (30-day) is at its 79th percentile of 10 years.

risks: Hormuz escalation (severity 5, oil supply, shipping, risk-off)
Sudden ceasefire collapses the oil risk premium
Election outcome shifts fiscal and trade policy
what_would_change_my_mind: A verified ceasefire and reopening of Gulf shipping lanes

research.summary: Supply chains are under above-normal pressure. The NY Fed's pressure index is 1.28, at its 87th percentile of 20 years and still rising, consistent with Gulf shipping disruption. Inventories are lean relative to sales. This adds to goods inflation over the next one to two quarters.

key_findings.claim: GSCPI is 1.28 (September), at its 87th percentile of 20 years, up 0.08 in three months.
Inventories-to-sales ratio 1.33, down 0.07 in a year: little buffer.

risks: Freight indices not yet ingested (Drewry, Freightos)

research.summary: Crude is in a war-driven supply shock. WTI is $103 (up 66% in a year) and Brent $123, and the $20 Brent-WTI gap says the shortage is in seaborne barrels, while US supply is ample (Cushing 11% above its 5-year norm, output up 2.7%). US crude stocks fell 16.7mb in four weeks. Oil implied vol (OVX 57) is about 30 points above realized: premium is very rich, but a ceasefire could gap prices down. Natural gas is the opposite: storage is above normal and prices are weak.

key_findings.claim: WTI $103.37, up 66.38% in 12 months and at its 96th percentile of 10 years; Brent $123.10.
Brent trades $19.73 over WTI while Cushing stocks are 11.1% above their 5-year average: the shortage is seaborne.
US crude stocks fell 16.7mb in 4 weeks to 410.6mb, 4.1% below the 5-year average.
OVX 57.16 versus USO 20-day realized vol 26.7: a 30-point volatility premium.
Natural gas storage is 2.2% above the 5-year average and Henry Hub is $2.76.

views.statement: USO closes above 134 (about 21% below today) on its December expiry
UNG closes below 10.5 on its December expiry

risks: Ceasefire: crude risk premium could collapse 25%+ in days
SPR releases (17mb exchange offered)
what_would_change_my_mind: Brent-WTI spread under $8 or two consecutive large US crude builds
data_requests: CFTC managed-money positioning in crude and natgas

research.summary: Gold and silver are in a sharp correction. GLD is 28% below its 52-week high and 14% under its 200-day average; silver is 58% off its high after a speculative peak. The driver is rising real yields and Fed hike expectations, not a loss of safe-haven demand. Gold's implied vol is low relative to its year, so there is little premium to sell. Stand aside until real yields stop rising.

key_findings.claim: GLD is 28.3% below its 52-week high and 13.8% below its 200-day average.
Silver (SLV) fell 18.2% in a month and is 57.8% below its 52-week high; 20-day realized vol 42%.
The pressure comes from rising real yields (10y real 2.63%, +22bp in 3 months) and hike expectations.
Gold implied vol (GVZ 22.7) is only 1.4 points above realized and at its 15th percentile of the year.

views.statement: GLD closes above 302 (15% below today) on its December expiry

risks: A geopolitical shock could reverse the sell-off quickly
Central-bank buying data not yet ingested
what_would_change_my_mind: 10y real yield falling below 2.3% or GLD reclaiming its 50-day average

research.summary: The S&P 500 trend is intact but narrowing. SPY is 3.7% above its 200-day average and only 3% off its high, but Nasdaq-100 fell 6.7% in a month and small caps lag. Volatility is calm (VIX 17, curve in contango). The problem is price: with a CAPE near 41 and real yields at 2.63%, stocks offer almost no excess yield over bonds, so downside is more likely to be sharp than upside.

key_findings.claim: SPY is 3.7% above its 200-day average and 3.0% below its 52-week high.
QQQ fell 6.7% in a month (9.1% off its high) with 20-day realized vol of 22.9%.
VIX 17.2 with VIX/VIX3M 0.888: no stress in the term structure.
CAPE about 41 against a 2.63% real yield leaves a negative excess CAPE yield.

views.statement: S&P 500 stays within -9% / +9% of today through December expiry

risks: Tech leadership cracking (QQQ)
Rate shock from hotter October CPI
what_would_change_my_mind: SPY closing below its 200-day average with VIX above its 3-month index

research.summary: International stocks are underperforming as oil importers absorb the energy shock. Emerging markets fell 8.6% in a month and sit below their 200-day average; the Euro Stoxx 50 lags the S&P by 8 points over three months; China and India are down more than 12% over the year. Japan has held up best. EM implied vol (29) is well above realized (22), so premium exists, but momentum is negative.

key_findings.claim: EEM fell 8.6% in a month, is 4.4% below its 200-day average and 14.3% off its high.
Euro Stoxx 50 (FEZ) lags SPY by 8.0 points over 3 months; China (FXI) is down 17.6% and India (INDA) 12.1% over 12 months.
Japan (EWJ) is roughly flat over 3 months (+0.6%), the most resilient major market.
EM implied vol (VXEEM 29.3) exceeds EEM realized vol by 7.5 points.

views.statement: EEM stays between 52.5 and 71 through December expiry

risks: EWZ price history shows a 93% realized vol: data-quality check needed before using Brazil
Further USD strength hits EM
what_would_change_my_mind: EEM back above its 50-day average with oil below $90

research.summary: US stocks are priced near the most expensive level in history. The Shiller CAPE is about 41 (October 2026), above every month of the trailing 10- and 20-year windows in our stored history and second only to the 1999-2000 peak of 44.2. The 10- and 20-year averages are 29.4 and 26.2. Against a 2.63% real yield, the excess CAPE yield is about -0.2%, the weakest valuation cushion in our data. Modifier: US short-put size x0.6, max 12 delta. Global CAPE needs a data provider.

key_findings.claim: Shiller CAPE about 41.07 for October 2026, near the 44.19 peak of December 1999.
Stored history (to September 2023) gives a 10-year average of 29.4, 20-year 26.2 and long-run 17.4.
Excess CAPE yield = 1/41.07 - 2.63% real yield, about -0.2%.

risks: CAPE history after Sept 2023 not stored (source blocked); percentile uses 10y/20y windows ending then
what_would_change_my_mind: Real yields falling below 1.5% would restore some cushion
data_requests: Allow shillerdata.com or multpl.com in network settings
Global CAPE provider (World, ex-US, EM, countries)

research.summary: Option premium is richest in oil and emerging markets and thinnest in gold. USO implied vol exceeds realized by 30 points, EEM by 7.5, SPX by 5.6 and gold by only 1.4. Equity vol is mid-range for the year with a normal upward term structure. Oil premium is rich because the gap risk is real.

key_findings.claim: Volatility premium (implied minus 20-day realized): USO 30.5, EEM 7.5, SPX 5.6, GLD 1.4.
VIX at its 52nd percentile of the year, below VIX3M (ratio 0.888).
OVX at the 61st and VXEEM at the 64th percentile of the year; GVZ at the 15th.

risks: No option chains in the current data plan: strikes are model estimates
Election and payrolls inside the first week
data_requests: Option chains with Greeks (Massive options tier or IBKR)

regime.justification: Shifted 10 points from reflation to stagflation: the inflation impulse is a war-driven oil supply shock (Brent $123, Brent-WTI $19.7) rather than demand, payroll growth has slowed to 51k a month, and the Fed is tightening into it (2-year 73bp above Fed funds).

modifiers: Liquidity contracting (13-week net liquidity -$79bn): -0.5 on equity sleeves
Valuation: US CAPE about 41, far above its 80th percentile: US short-put size x0.6, put strikes capped at 12 delta
Geopolitics: severity-5 Gulf conflict touches energy: defined risk only, lower delta (cap 15)
Disagreement: desks contradict the playbook on gold, silver and natural gas: conviction capped at 0.5
Vol richness: USO, EEM, SPX have premium; gold does not (GVZ 15th percentile)
Event blackout: US midterm elections Nov 3 (72 hours, all sleeves); October payrolls Nov 6 (US equity, rates)

Stand aside: falling on real yields; gold vol too cheap to sell

committee.cio_memo: The book's base return this week is the collateral: about $1M in T-bills earning roughly the 3.88% Fed funds rate. On top, the committee sees a reflation/stagflation mix driven by a war-time oil shock, a Fed still tightening, and US equities priced for perfection. That argues for small, defined-risk premium sales where implied vol is rich (oil, EM, the S&P) and no exposure where we have no edge (gold, silver, natural gas). The risk engine blocks entries until after Tuesday's election. Under the current policy only the EEM condor qualifies; three more trades qualify if you approve lowering the minimum credit for single spreads from 20% to 10% of width.

red_team.challenge: A ceasefire is the biggest single risk: OVX 57 implies roughly 16% monthly moves, and a de-escalation could gap USO down 25% in days.
red_team.fix: Keep the USO spread at 10 delta, defined risk, max loss 1.2% of NAV.

red_team.challenge: In a risk-off crash the XSP put side, the EEM put side and the TLT call spread (bonds rally) all lose together.
red_team.fix: Halve TLT or skip it; keep condor puts far out of the money.
red_team.cio_response: TLT capped at $6k max loss; condor puts at 8-14 delta.

red_team.challenge: EEM momentum is negative (-8.6% in a month, below its 200-day average); a range trade fights the trend.
red_team.cio_response: Kept at $7.9k max loss; it is the only policy-compliant trade.

red_team.challenge: Strikes and credits are model estimates: no live option chains in the current data plan.
red_team.fix: Re-price every ticket on a live chain before approval.

red_team.challenge: Election on Nov 3 and payrolls on Nov 6 sit inside the first week of every trade.
red_team.fix: Enter after the election; enter XSP/TLT after payrolls or accept the event.
red_team.cio_response: Entries staged for Nov 4 or later.
